x: The course was trying, being very soft and wet. Traquair ran his usual race and Rollins gained experience from his run Rice found the going too much for him, after a promising start.

Then there is our star dancer, Rollins, who thinks dancing delightful, or so we infer from his expression. He gathers his lady lightly to him with his right hand and poises his left, clasped to hers, in the fashion of an artist Then away to the quickening sounds!
Our friend Rollins waltzed in 3rd. The first two got so much away from the rest of the field that, as seen by one of the "also ran," they appeared to be in a race by themselves.

Eighth place saw Tom Cotton finding some form, while Fletcher, eleventh, and Rollins, twelfth, completed the Belgrave team. Still, we had to admit defeat, as after totalling up we found St.

Flower ran his usual steady race and was only a short way behind his brother and Robertshaw. In a race of this standard it is creditable to finish in the first hundred, and Rollins, after starting slowly, succeeded in this.

Chorley ran well to finish 11th and Rollins and Eastman had a rare "dust up" down the straight, Rollins winning on the post. Dewberry, Duffett and Bayliss, with several others, thought that once round the course was enough and so were not included in the final reckoning.

We shall recall the Indolence that was Rollins' the Intrepidity that was Ring (he's had his teeth drawn now, though!), the Inscrutability that was Scrimshaw, the Immensity that was Ben May, and Illogicality that was Wright!
